path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLM and NLP/Text Processing with NLTK 3 Cookbook.pdf
about: A recipe-style collection for doing text processing with Python's NLTK library. It covers tokenizing, stemming, tagging, chunking, classification and working with corpora, with a short code example for each task. Each recipe is self-contained, so you can dip into the one you need.
readIf: Read it if you want quick working snippets for classic NLP tasks in Python without much theory.
takeaway: Most everyday text-processing jobs can be solved by combining a handful of NLTK building blocks.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLM and NLP/[MIT] Foundations of Statistical Natural Language Processing.pdf
about: A classic 1999 textbook that lays out the statistical approach to NLP before neural methods took over. It covers probability and information theory, n-gram language models, word sense disambiguation, parsing, collocations and text categorization. It is dense and mathematical, and it predates deep learning.
readIf: Read it if you want the foundations that modern NLP grew out of, or need a rigorous treatment of pre-neural methods.
takeaway: Language can be modeled with probabilities estimated from large text corpora.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLM and NLP/[Manning] Build a Large Language Model (From Scratch).pdf
about: A hands-on book where you build a GPT-style language model in PyTorch step by step. It goes from text tokenization and attention mechanisms through implementing the transformer, pretraining, and then fine-tuning for classification and instruction following. The code is meant to run on an ordinary laptop with small models.
readIf: Read it if you want to understand how LLMs work internally by coding one yourself.
takeaway: A GPT-like model is a manageable stack of components you can build and train yourself.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLM and NLP/[Manning] Domain-Specific Small Language Models Efficient AI for local deployment.pdf
about: A Manning title focused on small language models adapted to a specific domain and run locally rather than through large hosted models. It deals with choosing, adapting and deploying compact models efficiently. I could not verify the chapter details, so this summary is kept general.
readIf: Read it if you want to run a specialized language model on your own hardware instead of calling a large API.
takeaway: Small, domain-tuned models can be a cheaper, more private alternative to large general ones.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLM and NLP/[O'Reilly] Applied Natural Language Processing in the Enterprise.pdf
about: A practitioner book on building NLP systems for real business settings, using Python libraries such as spaCy and Hugging Face transformers. It moves from core ideas to building applications like text classification and entity extraction, with attention to getting them into production. The emphasis is on practical application over theory.
readIf: Read it if you need to ship NLP features at work and want a path from prototype to deployment.
takeaway: Pretrained models plus solid engineering make useful business NLP achievable without starting from scratch.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLM and NLP/[O'Reilly] Designing Large Language Model Applications (2023).pdf
about: A guide to the pieces involved in building applications on top of LLMs. It surveys how the models are built and trained, then covers adapting them with fine-tuning, prompting, retrieval and agent-style setups, and the practicalities of evaluation. The tone is overview-oriented, aimed at helping you make design decisions.
readIf: Read it if you are designing an LLM-powered product and want a map of the options and trade-offs.
takeaway: Building a good LLM app is mostly about choosing how to adapt, ground and evaluate a model for your task.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLM and NLP/[O'Reilly] Natural Language Processing With Python.pdf
about: The NLTK book, a gentle introduction to NLP through Python programming. It teaches text handling, tagging, classification, information extraction, parsing and semantics, with many exercises and use of real corpora. It teaches both the language concepts and the code.
readIf: Read it if you are new to NLP and want to learn it by coding small examples.
takeaway: NLP concepts become clear when you explore real text with a few lines of Python.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLM and NLP/[O'Reilly] Natural Language Processing with Transformers.pdf
about: A practical book on using Hugging Face Transformers for NLP tasks. It walks through text classification, named entity recognition, question answering, summarization, text generation, and techniques for training with little labeled data, making models smaller and faster, and pretraining from scratch. Each chapter works through a task with code.
readIf: Read it if you know some deep learning and want to apply and fine-tune transformer models on real tasks.
takeaway: Pretrained transformers plus the Hugging Face tooling let you solve most NLP tasks with modest effort.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLM and NLP/[O'Reilly] Natural-Language-Annotation-for-Machine-Learning.pdf
about: A book about building annotated text datasets, the labeled data that supervised NLP depends on. It covers designing annotation tasks, writing guidelines, running annotation, measuring agreement, and using the results to train and test models. The approach is the MATTER methodology of model, annotate, train, test, evaluate and revise.
readIf: Read it if you need to create your own labeled text data and want a disciplined process for it.
takeaway: Good models depend on carefully designed, consistently annotated data.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLM and NLP/[O'Reilly] Practical Natural Language Processing.pdf
about: A broad, applied tour of NLP for people building real products. It covers the general NLP pipeline, text representation, classification, information extraction, chatbots, search and other application areas, with industry-flavored examples. It is more about approach and pipelines than deep theory.
readIf: Read it if you want an end-to-end view of how NLP projects are structured in industry.
takeaway: A successful NLP product is a well-built pipeline, not just a model.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLM and NLP/[O'Reilly] Prompt Engineering for LLMs.pdf
about: A guide to writing prompts and building the prompt-assembly code around LLM applications. It explains how models read prompts, how to structure context, and how to handle things like retrieval, tools and agents. The authors approach it as software design for the model's inputs and outputs.
readIf: Read it if you are building LLM features and want to design prompts and context in a principled way.
takeaway: Think of a prompt as a document the model continues, and design it so the best continuation is the one you want.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLM and NLP/[Springer] Deep Learning in Natural Language Processing.pdf
about: An edited collection by Li Deng and Yang Liu that surveys deep learning applied to NLP. Chapters cover areas such as language modeling, machine translation, dialogue, question answering and sentiment, written by different contributors. It is more of a survey than a tutorial and dates from the pre-LLM era.
readIf: Read it if you want a research-oriented overview of neural NLP as it stood before large language models.
takeaway: Neural networks reshaped core NLP tasks, replacing hand-built features with learned representations.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLM and NLP/[Stanford] Speech and Language Processing.pdf
about: Jurafsky and Martin's standard textbook on NLP, speech and computational linguistics. Depending on the edition it spans from words, regular expressions and n-grams through classification, embeddings, neural networks, transformers, LLMs, and speech topics. It is broad, rigorous and widely used in university courses.
readIf: Read it if you want the definitive, well-organized reference for NLP fundamentals.
takeaway: Modern language technology rests on a coherent chain from linguistics and probability to neural models.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLMOps and MLOps/Generative AI with LangChain (2024).pdf
about: A Packt book on building generative AI applications with the LangChain framework. It covers chains, retrieval-augmented generation, agents and tools, and moving such applications toward production. The details vary by edition, so treat this as a general outline.
readIf: Read it if you want to build LLM apps using LangChain and need worked examples.
takeaway: LangChain gives reusable building blocks for connecting LLMs to your data and tools.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLMOps and MLOps/[O'Reilly] Building Generative AI Services with FastAPI.pdf
about: A guide to serving generative AI models behind web APIs using FastAPI. It covers wiring in language, image and other models, streaming responses, working with databases, handling auth, and testing and deploying the service. It combines backend engineering with model integration.
readIf: Read it if you know some Python and want to turn a model into a production-style web service.
takeaway: A generative model becomes a product once it is wrapped in a well-designed, secure API.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLMOps and MLOps/[O'Reilly] FastAPI.pdf
about: A guide to the FastAPI web framework for Python. It introduces the framework's concepts and then builds up to a larger example, covering routing, request and response handling, validation with Pydantic, dependencies, and databases. The final section works through a sample application.
readIf: Read it if you want to learn FastAPI to build modern Python APIs.
takeaway: FastAPI's type hints give you validation, documentation and async support almost for free.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLMOps and MLOps/[O'Reilly] Practical MLOps_Operationalizing Machine Learning Models.pdf
about: A book on taking machine learning models from experiments to operated systems. It touches on DevOps foundations, containers, cloud platforms, CI/CD, monitoring and the lifecycle of ML projects, with examples across major cloud providers. The authors lean toward pragmatic automation.
readIf: Read it if you can build models and now need to deploy and maintain them reliably.
takeaway: Reliable ML in production needs automation, monitoring and DevOps practice, not just a good model.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLMOps and MLOps/[O'Reilly] Python for DevOps_Learn Ruthlessly Effective Automation.pdf
about: A book on using Python for system administration and DevOps automation. It covers working with files and the command line, building CLI tools, testing, logging and monitoring, containers, cloud services, infrastructure as code and CI/CD. It is a general automation book that also serves as background for MLOps.
readIf: Read it if you want to automate infrastructure and deployment tasks with Python.
takeaway: Python is a capable single language for scripting nearly every part of the operations workflow.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/LLMOps and MLOps/[O'Reilly] What is LLMOps_Large Language Models in Production.pdf
about: A short O'Reilly report on operating large language models in production, the LLM counterpart to MLOps. It deals with the extra concerns that LLMs bring to the deployment lifecycle. I could not verify the finer details, so this is kept general.
readIf: Read it if you want a quick orientation on what running LLMs in production involves.
takeaway: Running LLMs reliably needs operational practices adapted from MLOps to their particular demands.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/Machine Learning/Deep+Learning+Ian+Goodfellow.pdf
about: The Goodfellow, Bengio and Courville textbook on deep learning. It opens with the math background (linear algebra, probability, numerical computation), then covers modern practice in feedforward, convolutional and recurrent networks, regularization and optimization, and ends with research topics such as autoencoders and generative models. It is theory-heavy and predates transformers.
readIf: Read it if you want a rigorous grounding in the ideas behind deep learning.
takeaway: Deep learning is learned hierarchical representations trained end to end with gradient-based optimization.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/Machine Learning/ML_basic_VN.pdf
about: A Vietnamese-language introduction to machine learning, apparently the book form of the author's Machine Learning cơ bản blog. It goes through core algorithms with the underlying math and code. I could not verify the full contents, so this is kept general.
readIf: Read it if you prefer learning machine learning fundamentals in Vietnamese.
takeaway: Machine learning basics are approachable when each algorithm is built up from its math.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/Machine Learning/Machine_learning_VN.pdf
about: A Vietnamese translation of Andrew Ng's Machine Learning Yearning, a short book on how to structure and prioritize work on machine learning projects. It focuses on practical decisions such as setting up dev and test sets, error analysis and diagnosing bias versus variance, rather than algorithms.
readIf: Read it if you want Ng's project-strategy advice in Vietnamese.
takeaway: Knowing what to work on next matters more than knowing another algorithm.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/Machine Learning/[O'Reilly] Fundamentals of Deep Learning.pdf
about: A compact introduction to neural networks and deep learning. It covers the basics of training networks, then convolutional networks, embeddings, sequence models, memory-augmented networks and an introduction to deep reinforcement learning, with TensorFlow examples in the first edition. It aims for intuition with code.
readIf: Read it if you want a concise, code-based path into deep learning.
takeaway: Deep networks are trainable function approximators whose different architectures suit different data types.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/Machine Learning/[O'Reilly] Hands On Machine Learning with Scikit Learn and TensorFlow.pdf
about: Aurélien Géron's hands-on book, first edition. The first part covers classical machine learning with Scikit-Learn, including training models, SVMs, trees and ensembles, while the second part covers neural networks and deep learning with TensorFlow. Every concept is paired with code and small projects.
readIf: Read it if you can program in Python and want to learn machine learning by building models.
takeaway: You learn machine learning fastest by implementing it on real datasets with solid tools.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/Machine Learning/[O'Reilly] Introduction to Machine Learning with Python.pdf
about: A beginner-friendly guide to machine learning with scikit-learn. It covers supervised and unsupervised learning, model evaluation and tuning, pipelines, and handling text data. It stresses practical use of the library over mathematical derivation.
readIf: Read it if you are starting out and want to apply standard ML methods in Python.
takeaway: Choosing, evaluating and tuning a standard model well takes you a long way.

path: D:/Books/AI & ML/Machine Learning/andrew-ng-machine-learning-yearning.pdf
about: Andrew Ng's short book on how to structure machine learning projects. It focuses on practical decisions such as setting up dev and test sets, choosing an evaluation metric, error analysis, and diagnosing bias and variance. It has little math and is made of very short chapters.
readIf: Read it if you build ML systems and want guidance on what to try next when results disappoint.
takeaway: Systematic error analysis and good train/dev/test setup tell you where to spend your effort.
